site.name: Humanities in Medicine
site.tagline: Exploring the human side of healthcare
site.description: A college club exploring the intersection of humanities and medicine.

home.lead: We are a student organization dedicated to the intersection of humanities and medicine. Through symposiums, our student journal, and community events, we examine how literature, ethics, history, and the arts shape the practice and experience of medicine.
home.heroImageAlt: Healthcare professional holding a patient's hand

pillars.title: Annual Symposium
pillars.description: Each year we host a symposium bringing together students, faculty, and clinicians to discuss topics at the crossroads of humanities and medicine.

pillars.title: Student Journal
pillars.description: Our peer-reviewed journal publishes student essays, creative writing, and reflections on medicine, health, and the human experience.

pillars.title: Discussion Groups
pillars.description: Regular meetings to discuss readings, films, and current issues in medical ethics and healthcare narratives.

pillars.title: Community Outreach
pillars.description: We partner with campus and local organizations to promote health literacy and humanistic approaches to care.

highlights.title: Symposium: Narrative Medicine
highlights.description: Keynote on storytelling in clinical practice, followed by student panel presentations.

highlights.title: Journal Issue Vol. 4
highlights.description: Our latest issue features essays on medical ethics, patient narratives, and more.

events.lead: A record of our past symposiums, speaker events, and club gatherings. Check our Instagram for upcoming dates and registration details.

items.title: Annual Symposium: Narrative Medicine
items.description: Keynote by Dr. Jane Smith on the role of storytelling in clinical care. Student presentations on patient narratives and reflective writing in medicine.

items.title: Film Screening & Discussion
items.description: Screening of The Doctor followed by a facilitated discussion on physician empathy and the doctor-patient relationship.

items.title: Fall Symposium: Ethics at the Bedside
items.description: Panel discussion with bioethicists and clinicians on end-of-life care, informed consent, and cultural competence in healthcare.

items.title: Reading Group Kickoff
items.description: First meeting of the semester discussing excerpts from The Spirit Catches You and You Fall Down.

items.title: Spring Symposium: Art & Healing
items.description: Workshops on medical illustration, poetry in hospitals, and the therapeutic role of creative expression for patients and providers.

items.title: Guest Lecture: History of Public Health
items.description: Professor Alan Reyes traced the history of epidemics and public health policy from the 19th century to the present day.

journal.submissionNote: We accept submissions from all students. Essays, poetry, short fiction, and reflective pieces related to medicine and the humanities are welcome.

officers.lead: Our leadership team organizes symposiums, publishes the journal, and builds community around humanities and medicine on campus.
officers.contactIntro: Have questions about joining the club, submitting to the journal, or partnering on an event? Reach out — we'd love to hear from you.
